subject: OBJECT-COMPUTER paragraph
notes: kb/Work PB78 / PB64 T5 (2026-08-19) + PB830 (2026-09-22). RENDERED (PDF p315 / folio 285): OBJECT-COMPUTER. [computer-name-1] [ | CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION ... | PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE ... | ] . - computer-name-1 is optional and the two clauses may follow the period directly, in any order, each at most once (a duplicate is COBOL2104 choice-alternative-repeated from 2002, the ONE choice-indicator reader, 5.2.6.4, and COBOL2423 at the COBOL-85 figure's separate brackets; counted by the ClauseCardinalities OBJECT-COMPUTER row since kb/Work PB3133, which also screens the COBOL-85 figure's cardinality and order; COBOL1652, the binder's own count, is deleted). The '85 format hung the clauses off a REQUIRED name, so the name-less clause form is gated below 2002 (computer-name-optional-2002, COBOL0900). CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION is LIVE (T5; an undeclared locale-name is COBOL1664). The format is CLOSED since PB830: the clause list ends in the `unrecognizedClause` error production (COBOL1970 at every edition - the pb830 negative), replacing the `~DOT` computer-attributes sink that swallowed `OBJECT-COMPUTER. IBM-370 WIBBLE WOBBLE.` in silence. The two '85 clauses ISO 2002 deleted, MEMORY SIZE and SEGMENT-LIMIT, are modelled `objectComputerClause` alternatives gated at their nodes; modelling them also fixed a rejects-legal-'85 gap the sink hid - the '85 printed order MEMORY SIZE ... PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE ... SEGMENT-LIMIT ... was COBOL0001 (the 85 golden, whose PCS must still take effect).
